_README: fp16 patch table for running Krea 2 on a Kaggle T4 (Turing / SM75, no bf16).
IMPORTANT: the find/replace strings below are UNVERIFIED templates. They were
written from notes, not from a checkout, so treat them as starting points.
This is safe: krea_server.py's post-load force_fp16_inplace() sweep casts any
bf16 tensor these patches miss, so a NO MATCH costs load time, not correctness.
To verify and lock them in:
1. python scripts/krea_server.py --probe     # prints per-patch match status
2. fix any '!! NO MATCH' find-strings against your checkout
3. set "required": true and fill in verified_against with the SHA
Once required is true, the server refuses to boot on a NO MATCH, which is what
you want long-term: a silently no-op patch is the failure mode that wastes an
afternoon. Until then it warns and leans on the sweep.

patches.name: text_encoder_dtype
patches.note: Text encoder load. Krea's T5/CLIP tower is the first thing to touch a kernel, so a bf16 miss here fails fast and loudly on T4.

patches.name: transformer_dtype
patches.note: Main DiT/transformer dtype. Biggest single win: this is most of the weight volume, so patching it avoids a large late cast.

patches.name: vae_dtype
patches.note: VAE decode dtype. A bf16 VAE on T4 typically surfaces as a dtype-mismatch at decode, i.e. after you already paid for the diffusion steps.

patches.name: vision_tower_dtype
patches.note: Vision encoder for reference images. This load path has no preprocess_sd hook, so it stays bf16 unless patched here or swept after load. Only matters for the _edit variants.
